title: Word Break II
summary: Insert spaces to form sentences whose words all belong to wordDict.

contractDetails.constraints: s has 1–20 lowercase English letters. wordDict has 1–1000 distinct words of 1–10 lowercase English letters. The source gives an answer-length bound of 100000 without specifying a byte limit.
contractDetails.output-checking: Compare complete sets of distinct strings. Require exact characters and single-space boundaries inside each sentence. Outer order is irrelevant.

statement: Insert spaces to form sentences whose words all belong to wordDict. Preserve every character and its position relative to the others. A dictionary word may be used repeatedly. Return all distinct sentences, in any order, with one space between words and none at the ends.

examples.explanation: The whole word and the two-word split are both legal.
The same word can be used twice.
No dictionary word covers the trailing x.

constraints: s has 1–20 lowercase English letters. wordDict has 1–1000 distinct words of 1–10 lowercase English letters. The source gives an answer-length bound of 100000 without specifying a byte limit.
hints: Conceptual: Each chosen word must match a prefix of the remaining text.
Directional: Precompute which suffixes can be completed.
Implementation: Store valid word endpoints at each position. Backtrack only through an endpoint whose remaining suffix is feasible, joining complete paths into sentences.
complexityAnalysis: O(nDL + nP + S) time and O(n²) auxiliary space excluding output, where D is dictionary size, L is maximum word length, P is the number of explored viable prefixes, and S is the total output length.
